steps.say: This lesson shows how to make sure a change is right: which check covers which part, and where each one lives. Nothing here is run except one small, read-only check.
Start small and fast, and go bigger only when you need to. That means compiling first, then checks that run on the build machine, then a VM, and the long suite last.
**A kernel change:** compile it first. scripts/kbuild.sh builds only the kernel and shows only the errors. scripts/shell-build.sh does the same for the desktop, os-shell.

Then `make test`. It builds the image and boots it twice in QEMU, once with UEFI and once with BIOS. Each line in this list must appear in the boot's serial log, the text the system prints as it starts.
The last line comes from init's test mode: about two hundred self-tests of the kernel, file systems, permissions, sockets and more. Each prints a `utest:` line, ok or FAILED.

steps.say: **A design change** (a theme, Facet's engine): tests/fm-dump.sh runs the Facet engine on the build machine, with no VM, and prints the laid-out tree. scripts/fm-check.sh runs it over every sample design.

steps.say: **A Facet 2 app** (a .facet file): `facet check` reads it and lists every error without running it. tests/facet.sh builds this tool into build/host/facet.
This check only reads. Here it checks the sample Notes app.
It answers "ok", with a count of the app's parts, or the errors it found. If the checker's own code has changed, rebuild it first with tests/facet.sh.

steps.say: **A change you can see on the desktop:** the `*_vm_win.py` tests boot the real image in Windows QEMU and use it as a person would. tests/vmkit.py is what they all share.

steps.say: It hands the VM a design and a mind through fw_cfg, the QEMU feature that kernel/main.c reads at boot. The mind is tests/fake_ai.py, a stand-in AI that answers from a script, so tests repeat exactly.
Keys and clicks go in through QMP, QEMU's control socket, never through the real mouse. Then the test waits for a line in the serial log. That is how a test knows something happened.

steps.say: A typical test, the lock screen. Each one says at the top what it checks and how to run it: here `python tests\lock_vm_win.py`. Look for the test named after the part you changed.
**Before you call a feature done:** scripts/feature_checks.py runs the whole end-to-end suite, one VM per run, for about an hour. The Feature tests gadget watches it.
Builds and VM runs are slow, and each test VM takes 12 GB of memory by default, so start them on purpose. Next: **15 The gadgets**, the panels that run and watch these checks.
